papers.title: Irreversible functional network deformation induced by preprocessing scheme order in multivariate EEG recordings.
papers.summary: The study quantitatively compared two EEG preprocessing schemes differing in the order of filtering and re-referencing, using sleep recordings, synthetic models, and surrogate testing. It found that re-referencing before filtering induces spurious cross-correlations that increase with frequency band and become irreversible for steep-spectrum signals (beta >= 2), while filtering before re-referencing introduces only small, correctable shifts.

papers.title: Inhibition of Cerebellar Dentate Nucleus-Zona Incerta Glutamatergic Circuit Improves Sleep Disturbances in Chronic Temporal Lobe Epilepsy Model.
papers.summary: Using optogenetic and chemogenetic inhibition of the cerebellar dentate nucleus-zona incerta glutamatergic circuit in a pilocarpine mouse model of chronic temporal lobe epilepsy, the study found reduced sleep fragmentation, increased sleep duration, and improved sleep quality. The authors propose targeting this circuit as a therapeutic strategy for TLE-associated sleep disturbances.

papers.title: Sleep-dependent modulation of thalamic brain temperature estimates in humans
papers.summary: The study validated metabolite-cycled MRS for non-invasive brain temperature estimation and re-analyzed thalamic MRS data from young adults who slept in the scanner. NREM sleep entry reduced estimated thalamic temperature by 0.2 degrees Celsius, with deeper NREM sleep associated with greater decreases, suggesting an evening nap lowers thalamic temperature.

papers.title: Pharmacological Inhibition of Histamine N-Methyltransferase Markedly Improves Hypersomnia in a Mouse Model of Parkinson's Disease.
papers.summary: In a 6-hydroxydopamine mouse model of Parkinson's disease, pharmacological inhibition of histamine N-methyltransferase with metoprine robustly increased wakefulness, reduced NREM and REM sleep, prolonged sleep latency, and consolidated wakefulness more effectively than other wake-promoting agents. The findings suggest HNMT inhibition as a promising therapeutic approach for excessive daytime sleepiness in PD.

papers.title: From spectral parameterization to spectral staging in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: The paper proposes moving from spectral parameterization to spectral staging in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder, though no abstract was provided and no concrete results are reported in the supplied text.

papers.title: Hyperglycaemia reversibly disrupts circadian behaviour in mice
papers.summary: Using an inducible mouse model of diabetes, the study showed that hyperglycaemia reversibly reduced the amplitude of circadian rest-activity rhythms by 50%, shortened the free-running period, delayed activity onset, and slowed re-entrainment after simulated jet lag. Restoring normoglycaemia reversed these effects, and brain glucose and O-GlcNAcylation were elevated, linking peripheral hyperglycaemia to altered brain metabolic state.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation impairs ventral hippocampus-medial prefrontal connectivity and task learning in rats.
papers.summary: Using simultaneous ventral hippocampus and medial prefrontal cortex LFP recordings during a T-maze task in rats, the study applied dynamic causal modeling and found that learning strengthened vHPC-to-mPFC forward connectivity while weakening mPFC-to-vHPC backward connectivity; sleep deprivation impaired this forward connectivity and produced slower learning and lower task accuracy.

papers.title: White noise as a non-pharmacological intervention for enhancing the recovery of rats with wound-associated sleep disorders.
papers.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
papers.summary: In a rat model of wound-associated sleep disorders induced by para-chlorophenylalanine and full-thickness skin excision, white noise intervention reduced sleep latency and inflammatory markers, increased sleep duration, body weight gain, and wound healing rate, and led to newly formed tissue more closely resembling normal skin compared to controls. The results indicate white noise promotes long-term sleep restoration and facilitates inflammation resolution and wound repair.

papers.title: Human-artificial intelligence collaboration for comanaging epilepsy in real time.
papers.summary: The authors developed an inpatient device platform linking scalp and intracranial EEG to a large language model-based AI that communicates with patients via a smartphone app, processing biomarkers of sleep, medication, cognition, and seizure probability. In 13 patients undergoing video-EEG monitoring, seizure detectors improved precision from patient feedback alone in a pseudoprospective simulation, without expert intervention.

papers.title: Loss of hepatic circadian organization in fatty liver syndrome identifies CLOCK as a regulator of lipid homeostasis in laying hens.
papers.summary: In a high-fat diet-induced fatty liver syndrome model in laying hens, time-series liver transcriptomics revealed a collapse of hepatic circadian organization, with rhythmically expressed genes decreasing from 1,046 in controls to 81 in FLS and core clock genes including CLOCK losing rhythmicity. Functional assays showed that CLOCK overexpression reduced lipid accumulation and lipogenic gene expression while increasing PPARα, identifying CLOCK as a central regulator of lipid homeostasis in FLS.

papers.title: Lighting and circadian cues shape locomotor strategies for balance and navigation in larval zebrafish.
papers.summary: The study defined distinct locomotor strategies that larval zebrafish use to control posture and navigate the water column under light and circadian cues. In darkness, larvae maintained balance with long, infrequent swim bouts with large nose-up rotations requiring utricular vestibular sensation, whereas in light they used short, frequent, variable bouts; lighting had a dominant masking effect while circadian rhythms modulated swim kinematics.

papers.title: Integrative analysis of Alzheimer's disease molecular networks with circadian regulators for prioritization of drug repurposing candidates.
papers.summary: This integrative computational study prioritized Alzheimer's disease drug repurposing candidates by combining network-based gene prioritization, transcriptomic similarity, and target bioactivity prediction, incorporating circadian rhythm regulators as disease context. It recovered compounds previously tested in dementia and identified novel candidates including PF-562271, MGCD-265, and BMS-777607 converging on FAK, PI3K-AKT, and RTK signaling pathways implicated in circadian regulation and neuroinflammation.

papers.title: A systemic circadian nicotinic acid riboside (NaR) signal engages the unfolded protein response and adipogenesis via the prefoldin complex.
papers.summary: The paper identifies nicotinic acid riboside (NaR) as a liver clock-controlled circulating metabolite that signals to adipocytes and neuronal cells, engaging the unfolded protein response. Proteome-wide stability profiling implicates the prefoldin complex as a NaR target, and NaR-induced UPR signaling converges on CEBPA to suppress lipid deposition under sustained exposure but enhance adipogenesis under temporally restricted stimulation.

papers.title: Respiratory event duration reveals novel phenotypes beyond the apnea-hypopnea index in obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: Using polysomnography data from 959 adults with obstructive sleep apnea, clustering that included longest apnea and hypopnea durations identified four phenotypes beyond AHI-based severity, including a prolonged-apnea phenotype with only moderate AHI and another with long event durations and pronounced nocturnal hypoxemia. Respiratory event duration provided complementary temporal characterization of OSA phenotypes.

papers.title: Night-to-night sleep variability and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality: a prospective cohort study with a complementary in vitro circadian-disruption experiment.
papers.summary: In 7,604 NHANES adults followed for a median 81 months, greater night-to-night sleep variability (midpoint, onset, and total sleep time SDs) and lower sleep regularity index were associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. Complementary HUVEC experiments showed that irregular dexamethasone schedules reduced core clock-gene expression, lowered Griess assay absorbance, and increased inflammatory and adhesion-marker expression compared with a regular schedule.

papers.title: Effects of General Anaesthesia on the Sleep Structure of Patients With Prolonged Disorders of Consciousness.
papers.summary: This prospective study compared pre- and postoperative polysomnography in 30 patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness undergoing spinal cord stimulation under general anaesthesia, finding impaired baseline sleep structure versus controls and that anaesthesia prolonged total sleep time without significant changes in sleep-stage percentages or CRS-R scores.

papers.title: Chrononutrition in the aging era: Circadian regulation of metabolism, resilience, and healthy longevity.
papers.summary: This review examines the molecular and physiological foundations of chrononutrition, focusing on interactions between central and peripheral circadian clocks, metabolism, and aging. It reports that aligning food intake with endogenous circadian rhythms improves insulin sensitivity, metabolic flexibility, lipid metabolism, blood pressure regulation, and inflammatory balance, often independently of weight loss, and may modulate aging processes such as mitochondrial function, autophagy, and inflammaging.

papers.title: Vortioxetine-Associated Rapid Eye Movement (REM) Sleep Alterations: A Focused Narrative Review of Human Polysomnographic Evidence.
papers.summary: This focused narrative review examines the relationship between vortioxetine and REM sleep, integrating sleep neurobiology, vortioxetine pharmacology, and limited human polysomnographic evidence from principally two studies. It concludes that vortioxetine-associated REM changes are best regarded as a pharmacodynamic effect whose persistence, dose dependence, mechanism, and clinical relevance remain uncertain, and have not been established as surrogate markers of antidepressant response or other meaningful outcomes.

papers.title: Does chronic occupational demand alter EEG stress biomarkers during cognitive challenge? a study of emergency physicians.
papers.summary: This study recorded 19-channel EEG from 17 emergency physicians and 18 non-healthcare comparison participants during rest and a standardized cognitive challenge to test whether chronic occupational cognitive demand alters EEG stress biomarkers. The challenge robustly produced frontal and posterior alpha suppression and increased frontocentral theta across groups, but no Group x Condition interaction survived correction, indicating an absence of detectable large group differences, with Bayesian analysis showing moderate evidence for the null for alpha and theta features.

papers.title: Impact of environmental enrichment and allostatic load induced by repeated mixing on the transcriptome of three porcine brain tissues.
papers.summary: RNA sequencing of hypothalamus, prefrontal cortex, and hippocampus from 48 gilts in a 2x2 enrichment and repeated-mixing design found that allostatic load induced 38 differentially expressed genes in hippocampus, whereas environmental enrichment had minimal transcriptomic impact.

papers.title: Time-Restricted Ketogenic Diet Combined with Exercise Improves Cardiorespiratory Fitness but Compromises Sleep Quality in Overweight and Obese Young Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated the effects of short-term non-energy-restricted and time-restricted ketogenic diet, alone or combined with moderate-intensity continuous training or sprint interval training, on cardiorespiratory fitness and sleep quality in 68 overweight/obese young adults. All ketogenic diet groups achieved significant weight loss (5.0-6.0%), and relative VO2peak increased in the sprint interval training (+13.0%) and moderate-intensity continuous training (+7.8%) groups, but all ketogenic diet groups exhibited elevated PSQI scores (12.2-29.8%), indicating impaired sleep quality.

papers.title: VAD-EmotionNet: a spatial-spectral attention network for EEG emotion recognition in the 3D affective space.
papers.summary: This paper proposes VAD-EmotionNet, a spatial-spectral attention network for EEG emotion recognition in a 3D valence-arousal-dominance space. It achieves competitive performance on the DEAP and DREAMER benchmark datasets using leave-one-trial-out cross-validation.

papers.title: A comprehensive investigation into EEG spectral analysis for ADHD brain dominance.
papers.summary: This study analyzed EEG spectral features to explore brainwave patterns linked to left and right brain dominance in ADHD, ADHD subtypes, and control groups. The Asymmetric Index findings suggest a differential power spectrum density pattern in ADHD subjects, with higher average PSD in the right brain during working states and in the left brain during resting states, and theta and alpha waves more dominant in the left hemisphere irrespective of task state, with theta notably prominent in the frontal region.

papers.title: Migration Characteristics and Mechanism of Active Components From Jieyu Anshen Granule in Different Insomnia Mouse Models.
papers.journal: Rapid communications in mass spectrometry : RCM
papers.summary: Using PCPA- and sleep-deprivation-induced insomnia mouse models, this study identified 89 in vitro and 43 blood-absorbed components of Jieyu Anshen Granule with tissue-specific distribution and predicted furanogermenone and curcumenol as core anti-insomnia components targeting ADORA2A, GABRB3, and SLC6A4.

papers.title: Prophylactic oral diosgenin attenuates acute sleep deprivation-induced liver injury in mice via modulation of the gut microbiota and vascular barrier.
papers.summary: After screening 265 natural products, this study prioritized diosgenin and tested it in mice under 24-hour rotating-platform sleep deprivation, which was associated with acute hepatic inflammation, increased intestinal permeability, gut vascular barrier alterations, microbiota dysbiosis, and elevated intestinal and hepatic LPS. Prophylactic oral diosgenin attenuated these hepato-intestinal inflammatory and barrier-related responses, and fecal microbiota transplantation showed partial transfer of the inflammatory phenotypes from sleep-deprived donors.

papers.title: Epilepsy in Children with Celiac Disease: Clinical and Electroencephalographic Characteristics and Outcomes in a Ten-Patient Case Series.
papers.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
papers.summary: This ten-patient case series describes the clinical, electroencephalographic, and follow-up characteristics of children with coexisting epilepsy and celiac disease. All patients achieved seizure freedom after a gluten-free diet and antiseizure medication, suggesting a favorable association but not causality.

papers.title: Which Domains of Cognition in Older Adults Are Affected by Sleep Duration? A Scoping Review.
papers.journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
papers.summary: This scoping review synthesizes 23 studies (2009–2024) on the relationship between sleep duration and cognitive domains in older adults. Both short and long sleep durations were associated with impairments in learning, memory, and complex attention, with gaps in research on social cognition and gender differences.

papers.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation for anxiety symptoms across fear, trauma, and disease contexts: a narrative review of clinical evidence and mechanisms.
papers.journal: European archives of psychiatry and clinical neuroscience
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes clinical evidence, stimulation parameters, safety, and mechanisms of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) for anxiety symptoms across fear, trauma, and disease contexts. Current evidence suggests taVNS may improve selected anxiety-related symptoms and autonomic parameters, but larger sham-controlled trials with standardized protocols are needed.

papers.title: Sustained Seizure Freedom After Stereo-Electroencephalography Without Definitive Intervention: Evidence for Network Modulation by Invasive EEG.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: Two patients with drug-resistant epilepsy achieved sustained seizure freedom after stereo-EEG monitoring without resection or neuromodulation, remaining seizure-free for 71 and 20 months. The cases suggest that sEEG implantation may induce microlesional or network-modulatory effects capable of interrupting seizure propagation.

papers.title: Integrative EEG/fMRI evidence for a multi-scale network underlying self-face and personal-object recognition.
papers.journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
papers.summary: This study used EEG and fMRI in the same 30 participants to investigate brain activity underlying self-face and personal object recognition, testing whether ownership processing is domain-general or stimulus-specific. Results revealed ownership-related activity across multiple spatiotemporal scales, supporting a hybrid model where stimulus-specific visual pathways interact with domain-general frontal self-relevance encoding.

papers.title: Sleep duration and prevalent osteoporosis among U.S. postmenopausal women: a cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2007-2018 with assessment of potential effect modification by physical activity.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 4,775 U.S. postmenopausal women from NHANES 2007–2018, a U-shaped association was found between sleep duration and prevalent osteoporosis, with the lowest odds at approximately 7.16 hours per night; high physical activity modified the association, with stronger odds for short and long sleep among high-activity women.

papers.title: Sleep disturbance and its associations with night shift work, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms among urban operation-supporting workers: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional survey of 3,667 urban operation-supporting workers in Chongqing, China, sleep disturbance prevalence was 94.1% among healthcare workers, 85.1% among environmental sanitation workers, and 92.8% among transportation workers; night shift work and anxiety symptoms were associated with higher sleep disturbance prevalence, with anxiety showing the most stable association.

papers.title: Circadian melatonin suppression and vitamin D deficiency disrupt aortic reactivity via MT1/MT2 and VDR-dependent mechanisms in rats.
papers.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
papers.summary: In rats, continuous light or pinealectomy combined with vitamin D deficiency synergistically enhanced phenylephrine-induced aortic contraction and impaired acetylcholine-induced relaxation, with dual deficiency upregulating MT1 (~10-fold) and VDR (~108-fold) mRNA, indicating circadian disruption and hypovitaminosis D promote vascular hyperreactivity and endothelial dysfunction via MT1/MT2 and VDR-dependent mechanisms.

papers.title: EEG-Derived Pain Threshold Index-Guided Remifentanil Titration During Laparoscopic Abdominal Surgery: A Randomized Trial.
papers.summary: This randomized trial tested EEG-derived pain threshold index-guided remifentanil titration versus conventional hemodynamic-guided titration during laparoscopic abdominal surgery and found no reduction in intraoperative remifentanil infusion rate (adjusted mean difference, -0.06 µg kg-1 h-1; 95% CI, -0.44 to 0.32; P=0.758). Exploratory secondary findings included lower PACU rescue opioid use and fewer PONV events through 48 h in the PTi-guided group, without reduced total postoperative opioid exposure.

papers.title: The Neural Symphony in the Periodontium: Health, Inflammation, and Regeneration.
papers.summary: This review characterizes the spatiotemporal plasticity of periodontal nerves and dissects molecular mechanisms linking neural signaling to periodontal immunity, bone remodeling, and repair. It highlights that neural equilibrium (e.g., CGRP and acetylcholine versus substance P and catecholamines) is required for periodontal regeneration and proposes nerve-targeted strategies including neurotrophin-functionalized biomaterials, local neuropeptide delivery, and bioelectric neuromodulation.

papers.title: Acute Onset Orolingual Choreoathetosis and Auditory Hallucinations in a Healthy Young Adult Following High Melatonin Dose.
papers.summary: A healthy 22-year-old man developed acute orolingual choreoathetosis and auditory hallucinations after ingesting 132 mg of melatonin following three nights of 24 mg. Symptoms resolved within 24 hours, but confounders included sleep deprivation and heat exposure; causality remains unestablished.

papers.title: Sleep disorder and residential segregation in Cleveland, Ohio: analysis of the index of concentration at the extremes (ICE).
keywords: Index of Concentration at the Extremes
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 165,669 individuals across 265 census tracts in Cleveland, Ohio, unadjusted models showed that residents of the most advantaged neighborhoods (predominantly White and/or highest income) had 25% lower odds of clinically diagnosed sleep disorder (OR=0.75). After simultaneous adjustment for all ICE measures and individual characteristics, only income segregation remained significant but reversed: residents of the highest-income neighborhoods had 11% higher odds of diagnosis (OR=1.11), possibly reflecting greater healthcare access and screening.

papers.title: Effect of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on perioperative psychological symptoms in patients undergoing elective thoracoscopic lung resection: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind trial of 176 patients undergoing elective thoracoscopic lung resection, four perioperative sessions of active transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) significantly reduced the incidence of perioperative anxiety versus sham (50.6% vs. 73.6%; RR 0.59, 95% CI 0.41–0.85; P=0.002) and was associated with improvements in depression, stress, sleep quality, and pain, with no severe adverse events.

papers.title: Possible Epstein-Barr virus-associated central nervous system involvement with reversible electroencephalographic abnormalities in a child: a case report.
papers.summary: A 5-year-old boy with fever, headache, and dizziness had normal brain MRI but EEG sharp waves; CSF targeted next-generation sequencing detected Epstein-Barr virus, and symptoms resolved completely with ganciclovir and follow-up EEG normalization, highlighting that EBV-associated CNS involvement can occur with normal MRI and mild CSF abnormalities.

papers.title: Dual-pathway processing of AI-generated Chinese ink painting: evidence from eye-tracking, EEG, and artistic expertise.
papers.summary: The study investigated how viewers process AI-generated Chinese ink paintings using eye-tracking, EEG, and semantic ratings, and whether artistic expertise moderates these responses. AI-generated stimuli yielded significantly greater scan-path entropy and beta band suppression than traditional and digital non-AI works, indicating broader attentional exploration and increased engagement, while professional and non-professional evaluators agreed on expressiveness but differed in cultural authenticity perception.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
